newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy car market needs admin, fiscal changes - Unrae.
newsitem.headline: Italy car market needs admin, fiscal changes - Unrae.

text.p: Italy's car buying incentive scheme has pushed the market higher but to maintain this trend when it finishes, revisions to administrative and fiscal laws are needed, Italian car importers' association Unrae said.
Italy's new car market rose 24.26 percent in the first four months of this year thanks largely to a incentive scheme started in January and set to run to the end of September, said Unrae.

Unrae sees the next four months of the year as less favourable and warns that there will be a problem when the scheme ends and there is no reduction in the administrative and fiscal charges for the private motorist.
Italy's new car incentive scheme financed by the government and car industry offers new buyer discounts if they trade in cars more than than 10 years old for a new one.
Figures issued earlier by the Ministry of Transport showed Italian new car registration rose 52.37 percent to 231,500 units in April compared with 151,933 in April 1996.
